sentences.text: ORAL ORDER Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties.

2. Learned advocate for the appellant - Mr.Nanavaty mainly quarrels with the impugned judgment and award on the ground that deceased was traveling in goods vehicle at the relevant time without goods carriage vehicle.
This is a fundamental and statutory breach of Section 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

He would further submit that as the goods carrying vehicle is not permitted to carry the passenger; however looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence, it is established that deceased travelling as passenger in the goods vehicle.

He would further submit that when the claimants have tried to put such a case that deceased was travelling in Tempo with five live stocks (buffalo), no evidence to that effect has been led before the tribunal.
He would submit that tribunal did not consider the same and erred in earmarking the liability of the insurance company to pay the compensation.
2.1 By making above submissions, learned advocate for the appellant submits to dismiss this appeal.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned advocate for the claimant would submit to dismiss this appeal on the ground that there is no merit in the appeal.
He would submit that deceased was travelling alongwith five buffalo and therefore there is no statutory or fundamental breach which has rightly been noted by the tribunal.
By making above submissions, he would submit to dismiss the present appeal.
4. Regard being had to the rival contentions of learned advocate for both the sides, at the outset, let refer to the finding and observations made by the tribunal in regards to issue no.1.

"11. As per the oral testimony of widow Menaben it been proved that on 22-7-1999 deceased has Dashrathbhai was travelling in a Truck No.GJ-2/V-4010 and due to bursting of tyre, the truck was dashed with the tree at the road side.

As a result,
accident was arised and deceased was died on the spot.
Therefore, considering the panchnama place of accident, the truck was lying at the place and five buffaloes were also found at the rear side of the truck in a dead position.

Therefore, though deceased Menaben has no personal knowledge with regard to manner of but looking to the physical facts of the narrated in the panchnama the reasonable would arise that deceased was travelling in a truck and he was died due to said accident.

Therefore,
the principle "Res Ipsa Loquitur" would apply and nok burden shifts upon the opponents to prove that there was no any negligent driving on the part of the truck driver.
Opponents have not discharged their burden.

any rebuttal evidence, raised adverse inference against the opponents holding that the truck in question was driven by its driver in a careless manner and before journey the driver was failed to check the conditions of the tyres which suggest that the driver was NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1143/2011 ORDER DATED: 09/10/2024 undefined negligent to keep the vehicle in a road worthy.

Therefore, I hold issue No. in affirmative."
5.
What further appears that accident occurred due to bursting of tyre and therefore the driver of the truck lost control over the steering and went into the ditch to dash with the tree.

sentences.text: Panchnama of the spot (Exh.24), indicates that five buffalo were died due to this road accident and they were live on the carriage part of the truck.

Thus,
the tribunal has rightly drawn the inference that deceased was travelling alongwith his five buffalo upon the principle of Res Ipsa Loquitur.
This met with the inference drawn by the tribunal in absence of any rebuttal evidence by other side to discharge the burden.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the tribunal did not commit any error in drawing the inference that the deceased was travelling in the goods vehicle alongwith five buffalo.
6. For the foregoing reasons, I do not find any reason to entertain this appeal.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
R & P be sent back.
